surviving.title: Referrer 的父目錄是 symlink 時，Master 自己會被 lstat 判成「違規的真目錄」，而 auto-repair 會刪掉它（唯一副本）
surviving.claim: spec 說「一次 symlink_metadata 就判得出來」，但 symlink_metadata 只看 leaf。當 `.agents/skills` 本身是 symlink（stow/dotfiles，或使用者手動 `ln -s .aghub .agents/skills` 想「自己修好」），`.agents/skills/<name>` 的 lstat 回報 **file_type().is_symlink() == false、is_dir() == true**，正是 spec 定義的違規形狀「a real directory」；但它與 `.aghub/<name>` 是同一個 inode。接著走 Policy 2：「Both copies hash equal → collapse back to the symlink silently」—— 兩邊是同一個目錄，hash 必然相等，於是「安全地」把它折疊掉，而 remove_dir_all 會穿過 symlink 父目錄把 Master 刪光。spec 的兩個合法分支(absent / symlink→master)沒有「resolved path 等於 Master 的真目錄」這個桶，而這個桶就是資料遺失的桶。順帶一提，spec 說一次 symlink_metadata 就夠也不成立：要判「resolving to .aghub/<name>」至少要 read_link(一跳，相對/絕對兩種寫法都要處理)或 canonicalize(整條鏈)。
surviving.why_spec_is_wrong: Contract 段「Any other shape — a real directory, a symlink resolving elsewhere, a dangling link — is a violation. One `symlink_metadata` per Referrer decides it. There are no heuristics and no unclassifiable states」把 aliasing 誤分類成違規；Policy 2 的守門條件是「hash 相等」，而 aliasing 下 hash 必定相等 —— 這條守門對這個狀態完全不設防，且它保護的正是 spec 自己寫的「Never remove_dir_all the sole copy」。spec 的 Link target 段已經想到 `.agents` 可能是 symlink(stow)，但只在**寫入路徑**處理，偵測路徑沒有。
surviving.fix: 在 hash 比較之前先做身份比對:對 Referrer 與 Master 兩邊都跑 `skill::lock::resolve_existing`(或 unix 上比 dev+ino);相等 → 判為 alias，**拒絕並指名是哪個父目錄是 symlink**，絕不刪除。並且把 Contract 的判準從 symlink_metadata 改成「lstat 判 link-ness + resolve 判 target」，同時明文寫出第三種形狀 aliased-master。另外 `crates/core/src/skills/install_fetched.rs:437` 現成的 `Linker::is_link(canonical)` 守衛有一模一樣的盲點(它只看 leaf)，實作者照抄這個 pattern 會把盲點一起繼承。反向變體(使用者先建 `.aghub -> .agents/skills` 想「免費遷移」，migration 看到 `.aghub/foo` 存在且 hash 相等，於是把 `.agents/skills/foo` 換成 symlink，結果 Master 變成指向自己的 symlink)同一個 identity check 就能擋掉。

surviving.title: 「每個記錄在案的 Referrer」不存在:兩個 lock schema 都沒有任何 per-skill 的 agent 欄位,而「absent 是合法」讓遷移自己的失敗變成通過狀態
surviving.claim: invariant 對「every Referrer recorded for it」量化,但 `SkillLockEntry`(全域 v3)與 `LocalSkillLockEntry`(專案 v1)沒有任何欄位記錄哪個 agent 拿到這個技能;唯一沾到 agent 的是**檔案層級**的 `lastSelectedAgents`(最後一次勾選,不是 per-skill 授權)。因此可推導的 Referrer 集合只有「所有 agent × 該 scope 的 write_dir」,而在那個集合上「absent」是 spec 明文的合法分支 —— 於是「這個 agent 的 Referrer 不見了」與「這個 agent 本來就沒被授權」在偵測上**永遠無法區分**。最傷的具體狀態:遷移在「Master 已從 .agents/skills 搬到 .aghub」與「Referrer 尚未建立」之間中斷 —— Master 是真目錄 ✓、Referrer 不存在 ✓ —— invariant **完全通過**,而這正是 Policy 1 宣稱要攔的失敗(apply-update/source sync 寫進沒人讀的 Master,回報成功並更新 lock hash,卻什麼都沒送到 agent)。D6 自身也自相矛盾:同一列同時寫「creates a Referrer for every agent the lock records」與「Intent is unrecoverable from the lock (it records no per-skill agent set)」。
surviving.why_spec_is_wrong: Contract 與 D6 都把「recorded Referrer」當成既存事實在用,但它不存在,而且**沒有便宜的地方可以放**:(a) 加欄位到全域 lock entry —— npx `addSkillToLock` 用 `lock.skills[skillName] = {...entry, installedAt, updatedAt}` 整筆覆蓋,只要 npx 對這個技能跑過一次 add/update/check,aghub 加的欄位就消失(D4 明定要共存,所以這是預期會發生的事);(b) bump lock version 來乾淨加欄位 —— npx `readSkillLock` 對 `parsed.version < CURRENT_VERSION` 直接回 `createEmptyLockFile()`,整份 lock 被當空的,使用者所有 entry 一次蒸發。
surviving.fix: 先決定授權記錄放哪,再談 invariant。可行出口:(1) aghub 自有 sidecar,放在 `.aghub/` **之外**(例如 `.aghub.json` 或 state dir)—— 不能放進 `.aghub/<name>/` 內,npx 會跟著 symlink 進去做 folder hash,多一個檔就是 hash 漂移;(2) 或放棄「absent 合法」,改成 invariant 對「該 scope 所有支援 skills 的 agent」全量檢查,並要求每次 mutation 都帶 `-a` roster(doctor 那邊 findings.json 已經被迫走這條)。無論選哪條,D6 的措辭必須改掉,遷移的「每個 lock 記錄的 agent」要改成明確的「所有今天讀得到 .agents/skills 的 agent」。注意:findings.json#doctor 已經把「lock records nothing about authorization」列為 open question,但那是在問 doctor 的 label;這裡的發現是 **Contract 與 D6 的地基就架在那個不存在的記錄上**。

surviving.title: 「shape check 放進 mutation guard」放不進去,而且會在同一個 flow 內被重入呼叫 N 次
surviving.claim: spec:「All mutating skill flows already funnel through the one interprocess mutation guard; the shape check goes there.」有兩個問題。(a) 真正的 guard 在 `crates/skill/src/lock/guard.rs`,而 `crates/skill` 的 Cargo.toml **沒有** 依賴 `aghub-agents` 或 `aghub-core`,拿不到 descriptor,算不出任何 Referrer 路徑 —— 檢查只能放在 core 的包裝 `crates/core/src/skills/lock.rs:58 mutation_guard`。(b) 那個包裝是普通函式,函式體每次呼叫都完整執行(重入只跳過檔案鎖的取得),而巢狀取得在正常 flow 裡確實會發生:`transfer.rs:1851` 外層 guard,`transfer.rs:1906` 每一個 copy row 再取一次;`manager/skill.rs:271 guard_and_reload` 也在其下再取。也就是說 shape check + auto-repair 會在一次 reconcile 中對同一 scope 跑 N+1 次,spec 對它的冪等性、以及「repair 在 flow 中途改動磁碟」隻字未提。真正會在中途持有違規形狀的 flow 是**遷移本身**(Referrer 位置還是真目錄、新 Master 已建立):只要遷移內部有任何一次巢狀取得 core wrapper,檢查就會對它自己的工作發火。
surviving.why_spec_is_wrong: prescription 指定了一個做不到的落點,並假設 guard 取得 = 每個 flow 一次。此外 spec 沒說「refuse loudly」的作用範圍是**整個 scope** 還是**正在動的那一個技能**;若是整個 scope,一個內容分歧、repair 拒絕自動處理的技能會把同 scope 所有 mutation 卡死 —— 包含使用者用來清理它的 `delete`。
surviving.fix: 把檢查放在 `crates/core/src/skills/lock.rs` 的 wrapper,並用 DEPTH/最外層旗標只在最外層跑一次(或做成獨立的 `ensure_shape(scope)` 由各 flow 顯式呼叫一次,而不是掛在 guard 取得上);遷移那條路徑必須顯式豁免。同時在 spec 裡把拒絕的作用範圍寫死成「只擋正在動的那個 lock entry」,否則要說明使用者如何清理被卡住的技能。
surviving.evidence: `crates/skill/Cargo.toml`(dependencies 只有 serde/zip/skills-ref/walkdir/dirs/log/ignore/sha2/feruca 等,無 aghub-agents/aghub-core);`crates/core/src/skills/lock.rs:58-73`;`crates/skill/src/lock/guard.rs:290-336`(mutation_guard_with_timeout:DEPTH 遞增,HELD 已持有則 `continue`,函式體其餘照跑);`crates/core/src/transfer.rs:1851` 與 `:1906`(外層+每 row 內層);`crates/core/src/manager/skill.rs:262-279`(guard_and_reload)。作用範圍那點屬於 spec 措辭歧義,未實測。
surviving.reviewer_note:
先把弱的部分講清楚:(a)「guard 在 crates/skill,拿不到 descriptor」是稻草人 —— `crates/skill/Cargo.toml` 的確沒有 aghub-agents/aghub-core(核對屬實),但 spec 說的「funnel」任何人都會讀成 core 的 wrapper,沒有人會把它塞進 `crates/skill`。這半不構成發現。

(b) 才是真的,而且比原發現寫得更嚴重。核對:`crates/skill/src/lock/guard.rs:290` `mutation_guard_with_timeout` 的重入只是迴圈內 `if HELD.contains_key(&path) { continue; }` 跳過檔案鎖取得,函式其餘照跑;`crates/core/src/skills/lock.rs:58` 的 wrapper 是普通函式,完全不知道 DEPTH。巢狀在正常 flow 裡真的會發生:`crates/core/src/transfer.rs:1851`(reconcile 外層)→ `:1906`(每個 copy row 的 `_copy_guard`)→ `crates/core/src/manager/skill.rs:266` `guard_and_reload`,三層。所以 shape check 掛在 guard 取得上,一次 reconcile 會跑 N+1 次;若 Policy 2 的 auto-repair 也掛在那裡,就是在 flow 中途反覆改磁碟,spec 對此隻字未提。

**最致命的是原發現只點到、沒說死的那點**:遷移前的狀態就是「每一個 Referrer 位置都是真目錄」= spec 定義的違規形狀,遍地都是。shape check 掛在 mutation guard 取得上,遷移一開口取 guard 就會被自己的檢查擋下來 —— 而 spec 完全沒有給遷移任何豁免。這是大聲失敗(不是靜默),所以是 required 不是 blocker。

「拒絕的作用範圍是整個 scope 還是單一技能」那點原發現自己標了未實測,確實是 spec 措辭歧義,附帶提出合理。

surviving.title: lock 讀失敗時 invariant 與 lock-driven migration 都會靜默地「零筆 entry → 全部通過 / 什麼都不遷」
surviving.claim: invariant 與 D5 的遷移都對 lock entry 量化,但 spec 沒說用哪個 reader。現況兩種都在:`read_skill_lock` / `read_local_lock` 對 unparseable JSON **fail OPEN** 回空 lock;`read_global_lock_checked` / `read_local_lock_checked` fail CLOSED。最寫實的入口是專案 lock:`skills-lock.json` 是要 commit 進 VCS 的檔案,一個未解決的 merge conflict 就讓它 unparseable → 讀成空 → 遷移看到零筆 entry → 依 D5「no lock entry names them」把**每一個**真目錄當成外來物「left untouched and reported」→ 回報成功、實際什麼都沒搬,而後續 install 開始把 Master 寫到 `.aghub`,agent 繼續讀舊的真目錄。invariant 同理:零筆 entry → 空集合上的全稱命題恆真 → 「refuse loudly」在磁碟狀態最可疑的時候完全不出聲。更糟的是「改用 checked reader」也不夠:`read_global_lock_checked` 走的是 `read_lock_for_modify_versioned`,裡面**照樣**對 `version < CURRENT_VERSION` 做 old-format wipe 回空 lock,所以一份 v2 全域 lock 在 fail-closed 讀法下依然是零筆。
surviving.why_spec_is_wrong: spec 把「完備偵測」建立在「lock entry 集合」上,卻沒指定讀取語意,而現有 codebase 在這一點上剛好有兩套相反的行為,預設那套(fail open)會讓整個機制靜默失效。
surviving.fix: 明文規定 invariant 檢查與 migration 一律用 fail-closed reader(`read_global_lock_checked` / `read_local_lock_checked`),並且**版本過舊必須報錯而不是回空 lock** —— 至少在 migration 這條路徑上要另外走一個不做 old-format wipe 的讀法,否則 v2 lock 使用者的技能會被靜默留在舊佈局。
surviving.evidence: `crates/skill/src/lock/io.rs:44-71`(unparseable → log::warn + `SkillLockFile::new()`,version< current → new());`crates/skill/src/lock/io.rs:91-133`(read_lock_for_modify 對非 NotFound 錯誤與非法 JSON 回 Err);`crates/skill/src/lock/io.rs:186-195`(read_global_lock_checked → read_lock_for_modify_versioned,註解自承會套用 old-format wipe);`crates/skill/src/lock/local.rs:133-149, 176-196`(專案 lock 同構,CURRENT_VERSION=1)。

四處引用全部核對屬實:`crates/skill/src/lock/io.rs:41-71` `read_skill_lock_locked` 對 unparseable JSON `log::warn!` 後回 `SkillLockFile::new()`(fail open),對 `version < current` 也回 new();`:91-133` `read_lock_for_modify` 只對 NotFound 與空檔回 default,其餘 I/O 錯誤與非法 JSON 回 `Err`(fail closed);`:186-195` `read_global_lock_checked` → `read_lock_for_modify_versioned`,註解自承照樣套 old-format wipe;`crates/skill/src/lock/local.rs:133-149` 與 `:176-196` 專案 lock 同構,`CURRENT_VERSION = 1`。spec 的 Migration 段只寫「Lock-driven (D5)」,確實從未指定 reader 語意。discovery-findings.json 對 `read_global_lock_checked` / `fail open` 零命中,是新的。

surviving.title: Policy 2's "both copies hash equal → collapse back to the symlink silently" deletes content the folder hash is defined to ignore
surviving.claim: `compute_skill_folder_hash` is npx-parity by design: it skips symlinks (`crates/skill/src/hash.rs:120-122`), skips any directory named `.git` or `node_modules` (`:124-126`), never records empty directories, and hashes only relative-path bytes + file bytes with no mode/permission data (`:61-69`). So "both copies hash equal" is NOT "contents identical". The npx fork at `.agents/skills/<name>` — which per the spec's own interop table is written by `cleanAndCreateDirectory` + `copyDirectory` and holds bytes that exist nowhere else — can hash equal to `.aghub/<name>` while exclusively holding a `.git/` directory (a user tracking their own edits), a `node_modules/` tree, symlinks, and empty directories. The spec authorizes deleting exactly that, and says to do it *silently*. There is also a third outcome the spec does not enumerate: `compute_skill_folder_hash` returns `Err` on I/O and on the bounds guards (`MAX_FILES` 10_000 / `MAX_TOTAL_BYTES` 256 MiB / `MAX_DEPTH` 64 — `hash.rs:13-15, 92-96, 109-113`). The spec's repair predicate is bivalent (equal | diverge); the real predicate is trivalent, and the natural sloppy spelling (`hash(a).ok() == hash(b).ok()`) makes two errors compare *equal*, which routes the un-hashable case into the silent-delete branch.
surviving.why_spec_is_wrong: The spec states the safety rule ("Never merge, never `remove_dir_all` the sole copy") and then hands the repair a predicate that cannot decide sole-copy-ness. Hash equality was never designed as a содержимое-identity test — it is an npx wire-format parity function, and the spec cites it as if it were `diff -r`. Worse, BOTH branches of Policy 2 end in a delete: the equal branch deletes the fork silently, and the diverge branch ("stop, show the divergence, let the user choose") offers a user a choice whose either answer is a `remove_dir_all` of one of the two copies. The spec's own no-delete rule is violated on every branch of its own repair.
surviving.fix: Do not make repair a comparison at all. Move the fork aside instead of deleting it: `fs::rename(.agents/skills/<name>, .aghub/.aghub-fork-<name>-<ts>)`, then create the Referrer symlink. One rename, no predicate to get wrong, no branch that can delete a sole copy, and the user can `diff` the two trees afterwards at leisure. If a hash comparison is kept for the *reporting* ("looks like the same content"), it must be tri-state — `Equal | Diverged | Undecidable(HashError)` — with `Undecidable` refusing, never collapsing into `Equal`.
surviving.evidence: Read `crates/skill/src/hash.rs:42-130` (skip rules, no mode, bounds errors). Empirically verified with a temporary integration test in `crates/skill/tests/` (written, run green, then deleted): two directories with identical `SKILL.md` + `scripts/run.sh`, where the second additionally held `.git/config`, `node_modules/pkg/index.js`, a symlink `linked -> /etc/hosts`, an empty directory `emptydir/`, and mode 0755 on `scripts/run.sh`; `compute_skill_folder_hash` returned EQUAL digests for both. Command: `cargo test -p skill --test zz_tmp_hash_probe` → 1 passed.
surviving.reviewer_note: Citations all check out verbatim: crates/skill/src/hash.rs:120-122 (symlink skip), :123-127 (`.git`/`node_modules` dir skip), :129-147 (only `ft.is_file()` is pushed, so empty dirs are never recorded, and `meta.len()`/bytes are the only inputs — no mode), :13-15 + :92-96 + :109-113 (the three Bounds errors). The spec really does hand a bivalent predicate ("equal | diverge") to a trivalent function, and the destructive branch is the one a sloppy `hash(a).ok()==hash(b).ok()` falls into. BUT the reviewer's concrete scenario is mostly wrong and I had to fix it before letting the finding live: npx `copyDirectory` (vercel_npx_skill/src/installer.ts:462-500) dereferences symlinks (`cp {dereference:true}`) and `EXCLUDE_DIRS` (installer.ts:423) drops `.git`/`__pycache__`/`__pypackages__`, so an npx-written fork cannot contain a symlink or a `.git` at all — those require the user to create them post-fork. What survives, and is stronger than what the reviewer wrote: `EXCLUDE_DIRS` does NOT contain `node_modules`, while hash.rs:125 skips it — so npx itself copies a `node_modules` tree into the fork that the hash is blind to, and "equal" can be declared across two trees whose `node_modules` differ arbitrarily or where only one has it. npx also `chmod`s to the source mode (installer.ts:495-496) while the hash reads no mode at all. So the equal-branch `remove_dir_all` provably preserves regular-file skill content but can silently drop node_modules, mode bits and empty dirs. Not a duplicate: the discovery scan's own hash.rs site says "It does not break… None" and never raises hash-equality-as-identity, and interop's `data_loss_risks` covers only the *relink assumes symlink* case, not the *repair decided they were equal* case. Downgraded from blocker to required because no skill content is lost on that branch. The reviewer's rhetorical claim that the diverge branch also violates the no-delete rule is overreach — a user-chosen delete after disclosure is exactly what the spec means by "let the user choose".
surviving.corrected_fix: Two changes to Policy 2. (1) Make the predicate tri-state — `Equal | Diverged | Undecidable(HashError)` — and route `Undecidable` to the same refuse-and-disclose path as `Diverged`; never let two `Err`s compare equal. (2) The equal branch must not `remove_dir_all`; quarantine by rename. The reviewer's target `.aghub/.aghub-fork-<name>-<ts>` is unusable — it carries a `SKILL.md` at its own root, so `top_level_skill_dirs` (crates/core/src/skills/prune.rs:464-481, `is_dir() && entry.path().join("SKILL.md").is_file()`) would enumerate it as a skill named `.aghub-fork-…` once `.aghub` joins the scan set, and `doctor`'s orphanMaster would report it. Use `.aghub/.quarantine/<name>-<ts>/` instead: that scan is one level deep and `.quarantine/SKILL.md` does not exist, so it is structurally invisible. State the constraint next to it — quarantine lives in a dot-prefixed subdir with no `SKILL.md` at its own root, and store scans stay one-level.

surviving.title: D6 and the shape invariant quantify over a per-skill Referrer/agent set that neither lock file records — a literally lock-driven migration creates ZERO Referrers and the result passes the shape check
surviving.claim: The shape invariant is stated "for every lock entry `<name>` at a scope, and for every Referrer **recorded** for it", and D6 says migration "creates a Referrer for every agent **the lock records**". Nothing records that. `SkillLockEntry` (`crates/skill/src/lock/types.rs:9-57`) carries source/sourceType/sourceUrl/ref/skillPath/skillFolderHash/contentHash/refCommit/installedAt/updatedAt/pluginName — no agent field. The only agent data in the global lock is `last_selected_agents` (`types.rs:81-84`), which is FILE-level (one list for the whole lock, written by `save_selected_agents`, `lock/global.rs:142`), not per skill. The project lock is worse: `LocalSkillLockFile` is `{version, skills}` (`crates/skill/src/lock/local.rs:95-100`) and `LocalSkillLockEntry` (`:26-92`) has no agent field at all. So the two literal readings are: (a) global — every skill gets the *last install's* agent list, i.e. systematic misattribution; (b) project — zero Referrers for everything. In case (b), migration moves `<root>/.agents/skills/<n>` to `<root>/.aghub/<n>` and creates nothing, and all 10 project agents that read `.agents/skills` natively lose every skill in one command. The resulting on-disk state — Master real, Referrers absent — is an explicitly VALID shape per the invariant (it is the spec's own "installed, granted to nobody" happy path), so the detector reports it healthy and no aghub command can tell a completed migration from a catastrophic one.

The prescription's input does not exist. This is also the one place where the spec's two headline features collide: the shape invariant is advertised as total ("One `symlink_metadata` per Referrer decides it... no unclassifiable states") precisely because it enumerates Referrers from a recorded set, and the same spec says that set is unrecoverable. Totality is inherited from a source of truth that isn't there.

Migration needs that set UNION the agents whose descriptor read-paths include `.agents/skills` at that scope (they hold no link today — they read the directory directly — and are exactly the ones D6 promises not to break); `classify_agent` / `agent_link_need` (`crates/core/src/skills/linker/classify.rs`) is the seam that answers the second half. Then restate the shape invariant to quantify over that derived set, and add a fourth valid shape or an explicit migration receipt so "withheld on purpose" is distinguishable from "migration died before linking".

surviving.title: Policy 1 puts the shape check in the mutation guard, which is per-lock-FILE — so one `npx skills check` wedges every mutating aghub command in that scope, including the ones that would repair it
surviving.claim: Policy 1 says "All mutating skill flows already funnel through the one interprocess mutation guard; the shape check goes there... A violated invariant refuses loudly." That guard's granularity is one lock file per scope, deliberately: `MutationScope` is `Global | Project(root)` and its doc says "One lock per lock FILE... Per-skill locks are the tempting refinement and are deliberately not here" (`crates/skill/src/lock/guard.rs:67-100`). The core wrapper's signature is `mutation_guard(op, scope, project_root)` (`crates/core/src/skills/lock.rs:58-73`) — there is no skill name in it, so a check placed literally "in the guard" cannot be per-skill. The spec's own interop table says `npx skills update`/`check` re-runs `add` unconditionally for EVERY entry in `skills-lock.json`, so a single `npx skills check` violates the invariant for every skill at once. All ten guarded flows then refuse: `manager/skill.rs:271` and `:487` (add/delete), `skills/prune.rs:134` (prune-lock), `skills/resync.rs:125` (apply-update / source sync), `skills/rename.rs:295`, `skills/install_fetched.rs:402`, `transfer.rs:1851`/`:1906`. `delete` and `prune-lock` — the two commands a user reaches for to clean up — are inside the refusal. And Policy 2's auto-repair cannot rescue it, because an `npx update` fork holds *newer upstream bytes* by construction, i.e. the diverge branch, i.e. "stop and ask the user", N times.
surviving.why_spec_is_wrong: The spec picks the placement for a good reason (one seam, no hand-mirroring) and then inherits that seam's granularity without noticing it is scope-wide while the fault is per-skill. It also never says what the *repair* command does about the guard: a repair that must take the same guard the check refuses inside has no way in. The result is a design in which the most common npx interaction — the one the spec itself says will happen ("defending means fighting npx's writes forever") — bricks the whole scope rather than one skill.
surviving.fix: Keep the guard placement for the *span*, but make the check per-target inside the guarded span, keyed on the skill the mutation actually touches — the guard stays scope-wide, the refusal does not. Explicitly exempt the flows whose whole job is to clean up: `delete`, `prune-lock`, and the repair command must be able to run against a violated scope (a delete of the forked skill is a legitimate resolution). State that a violation on skill A must not refuse a mutation on skill B, and pin it with a test — otherwise the natural implementation (check the whole lock at guard acquisition) is what ships.
surviving.evidence: Read `crates/skill/src/lock/guard.rs:67-125` (LOCK_FILE_NAME, MutationScope::{Global, Project}, `lock_path()`, and the "per-skill locks are deliberately not here" rationale at :70-75) and `crates/core/src/skills/lock.rs:58-73`. Enumerated the guard call sites by grep: `rename.rs:295`, `prune.rs:134`, `resync.rs:125`, `install_fetched.rs:402`, `transfer.rs:1851`, `transfer.rs:1906`, `manager/skill.rs:271`, `manager/skill.rs:487`.

surviving.reviewer_note: Mechanics verified: crates/skill/src/lock/guard.rs:69-81 defines `MutationScope::{Global, Project(PathBuf)}` and its doc says verbatim "One lock per lock FILE… Per-skill locks are the tempting refinement and are deliberately not here"; the core wrapper is `mutation_guard(op, scope: ResourceScope, project_root)` at crates/core/src/skills/lock.rs:58-73 with no skill name. I trimmed the reasoning hard, though: half the finding argues against a literal misreading (a competent implementer puts a per-target check inside the guarded span, not at acquisition), and the spec's own claim that npx `update`/`check` re-runs `add` for every lock entry means the common violation is scope-wide anyway, which blunts the per-skill headline. surviving.claim: The shape check needs the Referrer path set, which comes from AgentDescriptor skill paths in crates/agents. `skill::lock::guard::mutation_guard` (crates/skill/src/lock/guard.rs:267-338) cannot reach them: the `skill` crate has zero dependency on aghub-agents/aghub-core, and the dependency runs the other way (crates/core/Cargo.toml:17 `skill = { path = "../skill" }`). The only acquisition point that can host the check is `aghub_core::skills::lock::mutation_guard` (crates/core/src/skills/lock.rs:58-74) — a DIFFERENT function with a DIFFERENT caller set. The skill-level one is additionally the floor every `modify_*_lock` takes (crates/skill/src/lock/io.rs:13, crates/skill/src/lock/local.rs:17), so it is not a mutation-flow entry point at all; it is a lock-write primitive.

There is no "the one" — there are two, at two crate layers, with different membership, and the lower one is unable to express the invariant. surviving.title: The shape invariant's own decision procedure cannot decide it, and "resolving to" certifies the two-hop chain npx creates — so doctor says `verified`, the mutation guard says healthy, and a later tightening silently strips an agent named nowhere
surviving.claim:
spec.md:53-58 defines a conformant Referrer as "a symlink **resolving to** `.aghub/<name>`" and asserts "One `symlink_metadata` per Referrer decides it. There are no heuristics and no unclassifiable states." Both halves are wrong, and they are wrong in the same direction — toward false-healthy.

(a) `symlink_metadata` is `lstat`: it returns a file type, nothing about the target. I ran it against the three shapes on the fixture `t/.aghub/foo` + `t/.agents/skills/foo -> ../../.aghub/foo` + `t/.claude/skills/foo -> ../../.agents/skills/foo`. A healthy one-hop Referrer, a two-hop Referrer, and a dangling Referrer all return `Ok`, `is_symlink=true`, `is_dir=false` — indistinguishable. Of the three violation shapes the spec enumerates, `symlink_metadata` alone detects exactly one (a real directory). "Comprehensive detection" as specified is not achievable by the call the spec names.

(b) The natural repair — resolve it — is what the codebase already does, and it is what the spec's own wording ("resolving to") licenses. `doctor.rs:236-243` (`inspect_agent_link`) compares `canonicalize(slot)` to `canonicalize(master_skill)`. `canonicalize` is realpath: it follows the whole chain. I ran it: `t/.claude/skills/foo` canonicalizes to `t/.aghub/foo`, equal to the Master, so `AgentLinkState::Linked` → `linkAudit.state == "verified"`. The same test appears in the install path (`manager/skill.rs:356-370` and `1219-1230`: `canonicalize(slot) == canonicalize(canonical)` → `SkillAdd::already_installed`, which is what `transfer`/`reconcile --add` report as `already_present: true`) and in the removal planner (`removal.rs:557-566`: identity-matched by `entry.canonicalize()`).

That matters because the two-hop chain is not hypothetical — it is the shape npx leaves behind on every write, and the spec's own repair policy preserves it. findings.json#interop claim 7 confirmed empirically that `createSymlink` (installer.ts:225-231) rewrites `~/.claude/skills/foo -> ../../.aghub/foo` into `-> ../../.agents/skills/foo`. Spec Policy 2 (spec.md:143-146) then collapses `.agents/skills/foo` back into a symlink to the Master when the hashes agree, "silently" — restoring shape conformance for the slot it inspected while leaving claude's link pointing through it. Every subsequent check passes: the mutation guard's shape check (Policy 1) resolves through, `doctor --verify-links` reports `verified`, `Linker::link` returns `AlreadyLinked`, `transfer` reports `already_present: true`.

The payoff arrives on the tightening step the change exists to enable. `aghub skill delete foo -a cline --yes` at project scope: cline's write dir IS `<root>/.agents/skills`, so `plan_symlink_removal` sees the shared Referrer, `entry.canonicalize()` matches `canonical_real`, `targeted` is true → it goes into `paths` and is unlinked. Claude's chain set `other_refs = true` from the same loop, so the Master is correctly kept and the command reports success. I verified the consequence directly: after unlinking the middle hop, `canonicalize(t/.claude/skills/foo)` returns `ENOENT` while `t/.aghub/foo/SKILL.md` is still a file. Claude is named nowhere in the command, `read_effect_after` is only asked about cline, and `doctor` had just said `verified`.
surviving.why_spec_is_wrong: The spec picked resolution as the conformance test and then claimed a non-resolving call implements it. Resolution is the wrong test for this invariant: the point of `.aghub` is that a grant is a per-agent, independently revocable edge, and an edge is defined by its stored target, not by where the chain happens to end today. "Resolves to the Master" is satisfied by a link that depends on another agent's slot staying alive — exactly the coupling the change is meant to remove. findings.json records the same chain as a *migration* hazard (linker site: "`Linker::link` sees a link that resolves to the master and returns `AlreadyLinked` — forever… the moment the user does the promised 手動收緊 and deletes `.agents/skills/foo`, claude/zed/windsurf dangle") and prescribes `read_link` for the migration only. The spec did not carry that fix into the steady-state contract, so npx re-creates the chain after migration and nothing in the specified detection notices — the guard, doctor, install and transfer all keep answering healthy.
surviving.fix: Define conformance by the STORED target, not by resolution: a Referrer conforms iff `read_link(referrer)` (one hop, resolved against the Referrer's own directory) names `.aghub/<name>`. `read_link` is also the call that actually decides all four shapes the spec enumerates — real directory (`Err(EINVAL)`), dangling (`Ok`, target absent), resolving elsewhere (`Ok`, wrong target), conformant (`Ok`, right target) — so it delivers the totality `symlink_metadata` was credited with. Then: (1) fix spec.md:53-58 to say `read_link`, not `symlink_metadata`/"resolving to"; (2) extend Policy 2's auto-repair — after collapsing a shared slot back to a symlink, re-point every per-agent Referrer whose `read_link` routes through `.agents/skills/<name>` straight at `.aghub/<name>`, since the retarget and the overwrite always happen together (findings.json#interop claim 7 mitigation); (3) give the chain its own name in `AgentLinkState` (e.g. `IndirectLink`) so `doctor --verify-links` reports it instead of certifying it, and change `inspect_agent_link` (doctor.rs:236-243) accordingly; (4) apply the same test in `add_skill_universal`/`add_skill_from_path_universal` so `transfer`/`reconcile` stop reporting `already_present: true` for a chained grant.

- The Removal section covers "every agent sharing the slot" — computed from write dirs in `classify`. Claude does NOT share the slot; it has a private Referrer that merely chains through. Not covered.

NOVELTY — narrower than the finding claims, but still in scope. findings.json linker scan, site `crates/core/src/skills/linker/mod.rs:368-389` (blocker), already records the chain AND already says in `change_needed`: "Separately, consider having `Linker::link` compare `read_link()` (the STORED target) against the requested target, not just the canonicalized resolution, so an indirect-but-resolving link is distinguishable from a correct one." surviving.title: The migration cannot be "called thinly from both startups" — neither surface has such a startup, and the spec's own alternative seam is in a crate that cannot see agent descriptors
surviving.claim: The spec's Migration bullet says the migration "is one core function under the mutation guard, called thinly from both startups — per AGENTS.md, not hand-mirrored." No such pair of startups exists. (a) The CLI has no startup: `main()` is `Cli::parse()` then `run(cli)` (crates/cli/src/main.rs:694-706) — a call at the top of `run` makes `check`, `doctor`, `get` and `coverage` take the interprocess mutation lock and write, contradicting AGENTS.md ("read paths are deliberately unlocked"), check.rs:496-500's own stated read-only premise for the `--write-result` guard, and doctor's read-only doc; putting it in each mutating command instead is exactly the hand-mirroring AGENTS.md bans. (b) The api's documented single launch seam is the wrong one: lib.rs:183-185 states "build_rocket is the single construction point for both the standalone bin and the desktop-embedded server, so this one change covers every launch path" — that sentence will send an implementer to `build_rocket`, which is invoked from ~39 in-crate test sites with only a tempdir `app_data_dir` and no `$HOME` isolation (crates/api/src/routes/skills.rs:3029-3035 is typical; crates/api/src/routes/coverage.rs:83-88 documents in a comment that it deliberately reads the REAL `dirs::home_dir()`). A migration hook there moves the developer's real `~/.agents/skills` into `~/.aghub` on every `cargo test -p aghub-api` / `just preflight`, which is the "do not pollute real home" rule in AGENTS.md Testing. The actually-safe api seam is `start()` (the desktop launches through it: crates/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/server.rs:2 and :35-38), and it runs before `rocket.launch()` binds, so no request can arrive mid-migration — but the spec names neither. (c) Startup can only ever see GLOBAL scope. The api takes `project_root` per request and the CLI takes it per command, so project-scope migration is necessarily lazy on both surfaces — a startup hook structurally cannot perform it. (d) The spec's own policy #1 already names the right seam ("All mutating skill flows already funnel through the one interprocess mutation guard; the shape check goes there"), but that guard lives in `crates/skill/src/lock/guard.rs`, and `crates/skill/Cargo.toml` (lines 15-29) depends on serde/zip/skills-ref/walkdir/dirs/… and NOT on `aghub-agents` or `aghub-core` — it cannot resolve a single per-agent referrer path, which the shape check needs by definition. The reachable seam is core's `ConfigManager::guard_and_reload` (crates/core/src/manager/skill.rs:266), which is currently a private `fn`.
surviving.why_spec_is_wrong: The spec answers discovery's "where does migration live, and who runs it?" open question with a mechanism that does not exist on either surface, and simultaneously points the shape check at a crate that cannot implement it. Following the sentence as written produces one of: a CLI that writes on read commands, an api that migrates the developer's home during the test suite, or per-command hand-mirroring — all three are AGENTS.md violations, and none of them migrates project scope at all.
surviving.fix: Delete the "called thinly from both startups" sentence. Migration runs inside the mutation-entry shape check (policy #1), for whichever scope that mutation touches, behind core's `guard_and_reload` — not in `crates/skill`'s guard, and not at any startup. That also fixes the scope problem (project roots arrive per mutation), the CLI read-path problem (reads never take the guard, so they never migrate) and the test problem (mutating tests already isolate HOME). Consequence the spec must then absorb: its shape invariant ("Any other shape — a real directory, a symlink resolving elsewhere, a dangling link — is a violation") is wrong for exactly one shape. A lock-named REAL directory at `.agents/skills/<n>` with no `.aghub/<n>` is the PRE-MIGRATION state; it must classify as "legacy, migrate now", never refuse, and read paths (`check`, `doctor`, `list`) on an unmigrated host must tolerate it. Add that row to the detection table.

judge.q1_decision:
**Backbone: the proposal's type-first angle. Graft: a FIELD, not a new enum.**

`LinkNeed::NeedsLink { agent_skills_dir, shared_with: Vec<&'static str> }` — empty vec = private slot. `NativeReader` deleted (spec already calls for it).

Why the field is enough (verified): every production bind site destructures WITHOUT `..` — `crates/cli/src/commands/doctor.rs:305`, `crates/core/src/transfer.rs:1743-1746`, `crates/core/src/skills/install_fetched.rs:689-693` and `:737-760`. Adding a field is a hard compile error at exactly the consumers that touch the path, and stays silent at the `matches!(.., NeedsLink{..})` sites that only ask "link or not" — which is the correct split. Criterion 1 is satisfied without a new type.

**Kept from the proposal, verbatim:**
- Compute sharing from **READ paths**, not write dirs. Verified: cursor (`crates/agents/src/agents/cursor.rs`) and opencode (`opencode.rs`) read `<root>/.agents/skills` while writing private dirs, so a write-dir computation under-discloses by exactly the two agents that also hold a private link.
- Delete `master_skills_dir` from all four entry points (`crates/core/src/skills/linker/classify.rs:117, 162, 176, 190`). Verified dead after the move: `classify_paths` uses it only for `reads_master`/`writes_master` (classify.rs:139-146), both constant `false` once nothing reads `.aghub`. The 9 broken call sites are the point.
- Drop `reads_master`/`writes_master` from `AgentLinkPlan` (classify.rs:34-43) and `auto_covered` from `AgentSkillCoverageView` (classify.rs:54-78); keep `dto_matches_shared_core_view_byte_for_byte` as the CLI↔API anti-drift test.
- Rename `universal_canonical_dir` → `master_store_dir` (`crates/core/src/skills/linker/mod.rs:15-27`) and give the shared `.agents/skills` slot **no function of its own**, so no consumer can hardcode it back.
- Fold `install.already_linked` into the installed set (`install_fetched.rs:756-760`). Verified today: a re-install leaves `install.linked` empty, so `linked_dirs.contains(agent_skills_dir)` is false and the row is `installed: false, error: None` — after this change that becomes the dominant re-install outcome, and the CLI ("already present", `commands/source.rs:1084,1098`) and API (`success: true`, `routes/skills.rs:1917`) already tell two stories about it.

**Added — not in the spec, the proposal, or discovery:**
`canonicalize_lenient` (`classify.rs:80-111`) must become a one-line delegate to `skill::lock::resolve_existing` (`crates/skill/src/lock/guard.rs:154`). It is literally the banned walk: it matches on `(ancestor.parent(), ancestor.file_name())` and returns `p` unnormalized when `file_name()` is `None` — and `resolve_existing`'s own doc at guard.rs:161-164 names that as the reason it uses `components()` instead. It also never calls `std::path::absolute`, which `resolve_existing` does first. `core` already depends on `skill` (`crates/core/Cargo.toml:17`) and `resolve_existing` is re-exported at `skill::lock` (`lock/mod.rs:18`), so this is a body swap.

This is load-bearing now, not cosmetic: that one function is the key for (a) the new sharing computation = who gets granted, (b) the removal verdict's `before`/`after` sets (`crates/core/src/skills/removal.rs:412`), and (c) transfer's protect set (`transfer.rs:1723-1727`). Discovery's prescription ("Keep the function. Replace the dying test with a DIRECT `canonicalize_lenient` test") is wrong once the comparison decides authorization. AGENTS.md's "one home for path normalization" applies here directly.

**doctor:** do not redefine `OrphanMaster`. Add a third resting state `Withheld` (master present + lock entry present + no slot for this agent), `is_issue() == false`, excluded from the `broken_links` note at `doctor.rs:680-696`.
judge.q1_rejected_because:
**Rejected: `ReferrerSlot` enum + `dir_ignoring_sharing()`.** Criterion 4 (minimum new concepts) and the proposal's own `gives_up` #1: the escape hatch means the compiler does not enforce anything the field doesn't already enforce, so it is a new type that buys a grep convention. Two-arm enums whose only difference is a `Vec` being empty are the "abstraction for symmetry" the criteria reject.

**Rejected: slot dedup + `agent_results.len() == target_agents.len()` assertion (spec §Contract) AND keying API rows by `result.agent` (proposal F3).** Both fix a bug that does not exist. Verified: `symlink_dirs` is NOT deduped (`install_fetched.rs:686-694`), `Linker::link` on 8 identical dirs yields 1 `Linked` + 7 `AlreadyLinked` (`linker/mod.rs:281-288`), and attribution is keyed by **directory** — `failed_by_dir` / `conflict_dirs` / `linked_dirs` (`install_fetched.rs:706-725`) — so all 8 shared-slot agents already resolve to `installed: true` from one linked dir. One plan per requested target produces one `AgentInstallResult` structurally (`crates/core/src/batch.rs` drives it per-plan), so the positional zips at `crates/api/src/routes/skills.rs:1915` and `:2598` stay correct with no assertion and no re-keying. A `debug_assert!` compiled out of release, or a runtime `assert!` panicking a Rocket worker, are both worse than the invariant the code already has. Criterion 3 is met by doing nothing.

**Rejected: discovery's "dedup `agent_skills_dirs` by `canonicalize_lenient` before the loop"** (linker finding, `link_agents_to_canonical`) for the same reason — the dedup is what would have forced the assertion.

**Rejected: proposal consumer-change 5's desktop group-by as a replacement for an existing FE bucket.** Checked: `universalSkills` / `universalSkillsTooltip` ("Shared with: {{agents}}") / `universalSkillsDescription` exist only in `crates/desktop/src/lib/locales/{en,zh-Hant,zh-Hans}.ts` and have **zero consumers** in `crates/desktop/src`. There is no FE hand-mirror of slot sharing to replace — the strings are dead. Deleting `isAutoCoveredByMaster` / the `autoCovered` bucket (`agent-capabilities.ts:71-100`) still stands; building the new group-by is net-new UI work, not a swap, and the `shared_with` disclosure belongs in the install confirmation the CLI already prints.
judge.q2_decision:
**Refuse by default, naming the co-affected agents and telling the user to name them. No new flag, no new policy type.**

`-a` already accepts a comma-separated list and `all` (AGENTS.md, one `AgentSelection` parser). So the refusal is actionable with zero new surface: *"removing this from `.agents/skills` also removes it from cline, warp, antigravity, copilot, gemini, amp, kimi — re-run with `-a cline,warp,antigravity,copilot,gemini,amp,kimi`."* Once they are named, no agent is unnamed, the existing multi-agent batch envelope (`core/src/batch.rs`) handles it, and the disclosure hole closes by construction rather than by a flag that promises to disclose.

**Collateral has one home.** Computed by asking `read_effect_after` (`crates/core/src/skills/removal.rs:396-438`) once per reader of the doomed slot — never by assuming slot membership equals loss. This is the proposal's insight and it survives verification: `before`/`after` are `BTreeSet<PathBuf>` of `canonicalize_lenient`'d entry dirs (removal.rs:404-428), so cursor's private referrer and the shared referrer both resolve to `<root>/.aghub/<n>` and collapse to one element — deleting the shared one leaves `before == after`, `changed: false`. Cursor and opencode are therefore co-granted but **not** co-revoked, exactly as the proposal claims, and only agents losing their last path get named. `remove_skill_planned` (`crates/core/src/manager/skill.rs:786-923`) is the single call site to change.

**Wire, aligned with the documented `outcome` vocabulary:** reuse `kept` (`success: true`, exit 0, entity still present) — its documented meaning is this state with "Master" swapped for "slot", so no new value hits `--json` and no consumer breaks. **But the `KeepReason` must reach `--json` alongside it**, because `kept` currently means "you lose nothing" and this new case means "refused for other agents' sake" — the same word for two different states is the kind of silent conflation criterion 1 exists to prevent. `RemovalPlan.shared_master_kept` → `shared_kept`, carrying the reason.

**`reconcile skill --remove` is unchanged:** keep the pre-first-write batch refusal, `UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION` / HTTP 422, per AGENTS.md. The `Collateral` computation runs in that same preflight so the refusal names them. Batching is transport and must not become a quiet revoke path.

**Non-goal disclosed, not designed around:** for the 8 project / 2 global agents whose only skills dir *is* the shared one, there is no "remove for cline alone". The refusal names that floor.
judge.q2_rejected_because:
**Rejected: `--include-shared` / `include_shared: bool` + `SharedSlotPolicy { KeepAndReport, RevokeAll }`.** Criterion 4: a two-variant enum threaded through `plan_removal` plus a CLI flag plus an API body field, to express something `-a cline,warp,...` already expresses. Worse, it reintroduces the exact hazard: a single flag that revokes seven agents the command never names is the disclosure hole with an opt-in sticker on it. Making the user type the agent list is both smaller and strictly more informative. (The proposal's own `gives_up` #3 concedes the flag also silently breaks CI scripts to `outcome: kept`, exit 0 — the refusal-with-a-list has the same exit code but a message that says what to do.)

**Rejected: `pub struct Collateral { agents, via }` as a new public type.** The two facts are already on the plan — the agent ids come from `shared_with` (Q1) filtered by `read_effect_after`, the path is the slot dir. A struct wrapping a `Vec` and a `PathBuf` is a name, not a guarantee. Carry them on `KeepReason::SharedSlot { agents, via }` directly.

**Rejected: the proposal's framing that `read_effect_after` "stays per-agent and only needs asking more often."** That is right about the code but understates a consequence neither the spec nor discovery names: after the change every referrer for a given skill resolves to the one `.aghub/<n>`, so the `before`/`after` sets are near-binary (`{}` or `{master}`). `changed` then fires only when an agent loses its **last** referrer. That is the correct semantics for this feature, but it means the AGENTS.md-documented "a private copy shadowing a Master DOES take something away" case collapses to nothing when the private copy is a referrer rather than a real directory — the removal tests that pin that behavior must be re-derived, not just re-pointed.

**Rejected: refusing at `reconcile mcp` parity.** Out of scope; the `reconcile mcp` unnamed-dir-sharer hole stays "verified, unfixed" as AGENTS.md records. Closing it is a second, larger change and mixing them buys nothing here.
judge.q3_decision:
**Split the proposal's answer: delete the flag, but do NOT move amp/kimi's write path.**

**Delete** the two branches (`crates/agents/src/descriptor.rs:188-192` global, `:206-209` project) and the field (`descriptor.rs:44`), plus `crates/api/src/dto/agents.rs:15` and `crates/api/src/routes/agents.rs:64`, and regenerate the ts-rs DTO.

Verified the flag can no longer mean anything:
- Only amp (`agents/amp.rs:98`) and kimi (`agents/kimi.rs:91`) set it.
- **Project scope is an exact duplicate.** Both declare `project: ".agents/skills"` via `define_skill_paths!`, whose asymmetric arm emits `root.join($project_path)` for read and write (`crates/agents/src/macros.rs:232-241`); the flag then pushes `project_root.join(".agents/skills")` again (descriptor.rs:207-209). `project_skill_read_paths` returns the same directory twice, today and after.
- **Global scope is a phantom read path.** Their declared global is `home.join(".config/agents/skills")` (macros.rs:224-227, HOME-based, XDG-blind); the flag appends `get_universal_skills_path()` = `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/agents/skills` or `~/.config/agents/skills` (descriptor.rs:263-269). Identical unless `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is set elsewhere, in which case aghub reads a directory it never writes.

The wire break is cheap and I verified it rather than assuming: nothing in `crates/desktop/src` reads `.universal` outside the generated `SkillCapabilitiesDto.ts:6`, and the `universalSkills*` locale strings have no consumers. Delete is a regenerated type plus two lines.

**Do NOT repoint amp/kimi's global write dir to `get_universal_skills_path()`.** Instead: give their global read arm **both** spellings explicitly (`home.join(".config/agents/skills")` and `get_universal_skills_path()`, deduped through the same `resolve_existing` from Q1), and leave `global_skill_write_path` exactly where it is. `get_universal_skills_path()` stays, now called from the two descriptors that need it.

That is behavior-preserving — today's read set is preserved verbatim, today's write dir is untouched — while removing the field that can no longer change anything. After it, amp+kimi's global slot is a genuine 2-member `shared_with` and Q1's computation is fed one resolved directory, not two spellings.

Test-table changes stand: `crates/agents/tests/descriptor_regression.rs` `test_skills_capabilities_universal` (~:1008-1045) deleted, the duplicate rows (~:1309, ~:1314) collapsed, and **write-path assertions added** — discovery notes those tables assert read paths only, and the write path is what decides where a Referrer lands under the new layout.
judge.q3_rejected_because:
**Rejected: the proposal's step 1 — repointing amp/kimi's global `global_skills_paths` AND `global_skill_write_path` to `get_universal_skills_path()`.** The proposal's own `gives_up` #2 states the reason and then does it anyway: the repo holds two contradictory claims about where amp and kimi actually read at global scope, neither is verifiable from this repo, and *under the new layout the Referrer is the sole delivery mechanism*. A wrong pick is total skill loss for two agents on every machine that exports `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, not today's harmless extra read path. Taking an unverified vendor-behavior bet on the write path, inside the change that makes the write path load-bearing, is the single worst risk/reward trade in the three answers. Reading both spellings and writing where we already write costs one extra `Vec` element and bets nothing.

**Rejected: the proposal's fallback — "delete the branches but leave the field as inert metadata, documented as inert."** A field that cannot change behavior will be read as meaningful by the next person, and `AgentSkillCoverageView` would keep reporting it as a fact. The fallback existed only because the wire break was assumed expensive; I checked and it is not (no desktop reader), so the reason for the fallback is gone.

**Rejected: discovery's recommendation to keep the field because breaking the API wire is "not worth it."** Same evidence: the break is a DTO field plus a regenerated TS type plus `routes/agents.rs:64`, with no consumer downstream.

**Deliberately NOT decided here:** whether the real amp/kimi binaries honour `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `HOME` at global scope. This decision keeps that question open *without a landmine under it* — the write dir does not move, so answering it later is a one-line descriptor change rather than a migration. The same class of question is open for opencode (`OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` / `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`), per discovery's own contradiction #1, and gets the same treatment.
new_risks_from_this_decision: STRUCTURAL — only ONE of the three proposals arrived. The input array contains a single object (angle: 'type-first'). This is that proposal reviewed against the code, not a three-way synthesis. Every 'rejected' verdict below is against that proposal, the spec, or discovery-findings.json — not against two unseen alternatives. If the other two exist, this decision has not seen them.

BLOCKER — spec Policy #1 puts the shape check where previews and every diagnostic surface will never run it. VERIFIED: dry-run takes NO mutation guard on both surfaces — `crates/core/src/manager/skill.rs:786-790` (`let _mutation_guard = if dry_run { None } else { Some(...) }`) and `crates/api/src/routes/skills.rs:351-367` (guard taken only when `req.confirm`). `check`, `doctor`, `source list`, `source diff` are unlocked read paths by design and take none at all. So a shape violation (npx forked the content) is invisible to a `delete --dry-run`, to the API delete preview, and to every command a user runs to diagnose it — the commit is the first thing that refuses. The proposal's F1(d) states the opposite ('manager/skill.rs:786 takes the guard for the DRY-RUN branch') and its advice to document a refused preview as correct is built on that inversion. The check needs a home the read paths also call, or the previews lie.

F1(a) correction, conclusion intact: `crates/skill/Cargo.toml:15-30` does have workspace deps (serde, zip, walkdir, skills-ref, tempfile, dirs), it has no aghub-* deps, and `crates/core/Cargo.toml:17` depends on skill — so skill cannot see agents/core and skill→core is a cycle. The seam is the core wrapper `crates/core/src/skills/lock.rs:58`. It is stronger than F1 claims: ALL twelve acquisition sites go through it (grep: rename.rs:295, prune.rs:134, resync.rs:125, install_fetched.rs:402, transfer.rs:1851 + :1906, manager/skill.rs:271/487/654/786/1168, api/routes/skills.rs:352/1131) — not 10. F1(b) stands: the wrapper returns `std::io::Result`, so a refusal cannot carry an `aghub_core::error_codes` value without a return-type change; there is precedent for the projection (`MUTATION_LOCK_BUSY_CODE`, lock.rs:38) but it goes through `ConfigError::Io`, which is lossy for a shape refusal that must name the shape.

NEW, not in spec / discovery / the proposal — the test hook that will manufacture false greens. `set_skills_path_override` is a thread-local holding ONE `(String, PathBuf)` pair, not a map (`crates/core/src/adapter.rs:13, 18-22`), and `TestConfig::drop` clears it id-blind (`crates/core/src/testing.rs:149-157` calls `set_skills_path_override(id, None)`, which nulls the whole slot regardless of which agent occupies it). Two live `TestConfig`s: the second clobbers the first's override, and dropping the first un-isolates the second. Harmless today. After the change, every agent is NeedsLink and cross-agent grant/collateral tests are the ENTIRE new test surface — so an overridden agent silently falls out of its shared slot and a test asserting 'installing to cline also grants warp' or 'the delete is refused for collateral' passes on override state rather than on layout, while the un-isolated agent writes referrers into the developer's real home. Do NOT extend the override into a map; sharing tests must isolate via `$HOME` or a project tempdir per AGENTS.md Testing.

NEW — the spec's `relative_path` prescription is half a fix. `relative_path` (`crates/core/src/skills/linker/mod.rs:106-135`) computes a common prefix over raw components; resolving `from` (agent_skills_dir) but not `to` (master_dir) makes the two sides disagree about their prefix. On macOS `/var` vs `/private/var`, or any stow/dotfiles `.agents`, that yields either an absurd `../..` chain or `common == 0`, which falls back to the ABSOLUTE target (mod.rs:116-118) — silently defeating the portability `LinkTarget::Relative` exists for at project scope, with no error on either side. Resolve BOTH or NEITHER. Both exist by then: `create_dir_all(agent_skills_dir)` at mod.rs:390 precedes the call at :394, and `install_universal` claims the Master before linking (mod.rs:228-240). Also note `LinkTarget::Relative` is live production (manager/skill.rs:405/1249/1496/1669, install_fetched.rs:843/896), so this is not dead code.

F2 confirmed against the spec's own text — the spec sends the implementer to the wrong place. `AgentLinkState::OrphanMaster` is gated on `!tracked` (`crates/cli/src/commands/doctor.rs:319-324`), so a withheld-but-installed skill (lock entry present, no slot for this agent) never reaches it: it reports `Missing`, `is_issue()` counts it (doctor.rs:107-116), `LinkAudit::Issues` fires `--fail-on-issues`, and the note at doctor.rs:680-696 prints `source sync --skill <n> --install-missing --yes` — the exact command that undoes the user's deliberate narrowing. Redefining `orphanMaster`, as the spec says, leaves this intact. Hence the `Withheld` state in Q1.

Swapping `canonicalize_lenient`'s body (Q1) changes six external callers' behavior in one commit, and two of them are safety-critical: the removal verdict's dedup key (`crates/core/src/skills/removal.rs:412`) and transfer's protect set (`transfer.rs:1723-1727`). Discovery's prescription for this function is 'keep it, add a direct test'. It needs the AGENTS.md Testing treatment instead: a test proven to go red with the old body restored (a symlinked tempdir root, and a path ending in `..` — the case where `file_name()` is None and the old walk abandons), not a test that merely passes after the swap.

Still undecided and now on the critical path: the spec's `.gitignore` question. Every project-scope install creates a new top-level `.aghub/` in the user's repo. Nothing in the three answers touches it, and this repo's `.gitignore` currently carries only `.agents/.aghub-mutation.lock`.

Verified-open, inherited from Q3: whether amp/kimi (and opencode, per discovery contradiction #1) read at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `$HOME/.config` at global scope. This decision keeps the write path frozen so a wrong answer is not skill loss, but the question is real and must be answered against the vendors before anyone touches those descriptors' write arms.

revisions.spec_section: npx `skills` coexistence → Policy 2 ("Auto-repair shape only, never content")
revisions.change: Policy 2 的兩個分支都以刪除收場，而它的守門條件（hash 相等）在最危險的狀態下必定成立：當 .agents 或 .agents/skills 本身是 symlink（stow/dotfiles）時，Referrer 與 Master 是同一個 inode，lstat 判成「違規的真目錄」、hash 必定相等，remove_dir_all 直接刪掉唯一副本（已實測）。另外 compute_skill_folder_hash 是 npx 相容函式不是 diff -r（略過 symlink、.git、node_modules、空目錄、mode），而且會回 Err，把三值判斷寫成雙值會讓 Err==Err 落進刪除分支。改成：先做 identity 比對，再用 hash 對照 lock entry 分流，任何分支都不 remove_dir_all。
revisions.replacement_text:
2. **Repair is lossless or it does not happen.** Classify the Referrer path, then act:

| shape at the Referrer path | verdict | action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| absent | legal | none |
| symlink whose one-hop target is `.aghub/<name>` | conformant | none |
| symlink resolving elsewhere, through another Referrer, or dangling | violation | retarget the link at `.aghub/<name>` — lossless; report the old target |
| real directory that `resolve_existing` (or dev+ino) says IS `.aghub/<name>` | **aliased Master** | REFUSE, naming the symlinked parent (`.agents` or `.agents/skills` is a link into the store — stow/dotfiles, or a hand-made "fix"). Never rename, never remove: the two paths are one directory, so every repair destroys the only copy. Verified empirically: `symlink_metadata` reports `is_symlink = false, is_dir = true` there, and `remove_dir_all` deletes the Master. |
| real directory whose `compute_skill_folder_hash` equals the lock entry's `skillFolderHash` | npx wrote it and nobody edited it | `fs::rename` it to `.aghub/.quarantine/<name>-<unix-ts>/`, then create the Referrer. Report the quarantine path. If the rename fails (EXDEV), refuse — never fall back to a copy-then-delete. |
| real directory whose hash differs, or cannot be computed | **legal shadow** (AGENTS.md: "a private copy shadowing a Master DOES take something away, and stays legal") | not a violation. The mutation proceeds and the result names the agents that will not see the write. |

Never `remove_dir_all` a Referrer path, on any branch. `compute_skill_folder_hash` is npx wire-format parity, not `diff -r`: it skips symlinks, `.git` and `node_modules`, records no empty directories and no mode bits (`crates/skill/src/hash.rs:120-147`), and returns `Err` on its bounds guards (`:13-15, 92-96, 109-113`). It may therefore never decide a delete — here it only separates "npx's own copy" from "something a human touched", and both outcomes are lossless, so an `Err` is treated as the shadow branch.

Quarantine lives in a dot-prefixed subdirectory with no `SKILL.md` at its own root, so `top_level_skill_dirs` (`crates/core/src/skills/prune.rs:464-481`, which requires `is_dir() && join("SKILL.md").is_file()` one level deep) cannot enumerate it as a skill once `.aghub` joins the scan set, and `doctor` cannot report it as an orphan Master.

After a quarantine the lock's `skillFolderHash` is npx's, not the Master's. Nothing new is needed: the existing auto-heal path (`write_auto_healed_hashes`, `crates/api/src/routes/skills_update.rs:180`) reconciles it on the next check. Say so, or it reads as silent drift.

revisions.spec_section: npx `skills` coexistence → Policy 1 ("Detect at every mutation entry")
revisions.change: 「shape check 放進那唯一的 mutation guard」在三個層面站不住：guard 在 crates/skill（看不到 descriptor）、core wrapper 沒有 skill 名字（只能拒整個 scope）、guard 是 reentrant 且 batch 每列重取、而 dry-run 兩個 surface 都不取 guard（所以 preview 與所有診斷指令永遠跑不到這個檢查）。改成 plan 時明確呼叫的 verify_shape，preview 與 commit 走同一條；並把「comprehensive detection」限縮成 shape，把 Policy 1 真正 load-bearing 的那半改用「回報送達了誰」來關掉。
revisions.replacement_text:
1. **Detect where the decision is made, not where the lock is taken.** The check is an explicit `verify_shape(scope, &names_this_command_touches)` in core, called by each flow at PLAN time — before the `dry_run` branch — so a preview and its commit always answer identically.

   It is NOT hung on a guard acquisition. `crates/skill/src/lock/guard.rs` cannot see descriptors (`crates/skill/Cargo.toml` carries no `aghub-*` dependency and `crates/core/Cargo.toml:17` runs core→skill, so skill→core is a cycle); the core wrapper (`crates/core/src/skills/lock.rs:58`) takes `ResourceScope` + `Option<&Path>` and no skill name, so a check there could only refuse a whole scope; it is reentrant and re-entered per batch row (`crates/core/src/transfer.rs:1851` and `:1906`); and previews take no guard at all (`crates/core/src/manager/skill.rs:786-790`, `crates/api/src/routes/skills.rs:351-367`) — the surfaces a user reaches for to diagnose a violation are exactly the ones that would never run it.

   A violation refuses only the mutation on the skill it names; a violation on skill A must never refuse a mutation on skill B. Pin that with a test — checking the whole lock at guard acquisition is the natural implementation and is what ships otherwise. Migration does not call `verify_shape`: it establishes the shape. `delete` needs no exemption, because under Policy 2 the fork is quarantined before the delete, so the delete is lossless.

   **Scope of the claim.** This makes detection comprehensive **of shape**. A Referrer that was never granted and one that was lost are the same on disk, and the lock records no per-skill agent set, so lost authorization is out of detection scope and `absent` stays legal — install and delete both pass through `absent` mid-transaction, and a later tightening of `absent` would break both.

   **The load-bearing half is closed by reporting, not by refusing.** `apply-update`, `source sync` and the install results name the Referrers the write actually reached, and say so explicitly when that set is empty. A write to `.aghub/<name>` that no agent reads then cannot report bare success with a fresh lock hash while delivering nothing.

revisions.change: 整段重寫：量詞改成可推導的集合（沒有任何東西「記錄」Referrer）；刪掉「no heuristics and no unclassifiable states」（absent 合法就是反例）；「一次 symlink_metadata 就判得出來」是錯的 —— healthy / 兩跳鏈 / dangling 三者 lstat 完全相同，而 npx 每次寫入都會製造那條兩跳鏈，它通過樹裡所有現有的 endpoint 比對（doctor 報 verified），直到一個只點名 cline 的 delete 把中間那跳拆掉、讓沒被點名的 claude 斷鏈。補上正確的兩次 syscall 判準與唯一落點；補上 lock key ≠ 目錄名；補上 legacy（未遷移）那一列。

### The shape invariant (this is what makes SHAPE detection total)

For every lock entry `<name>` at a scope, and for every Referrer path in the set DERIVED for it — every skills write dir of every skills-capable agent at that scope, via `classify_agent` / `agent_link_need`; nothing in either lock file records a Referrer (see D6):

- `.aghub/<sanitize_name(name)>` is a real directory — the ONLY physical copy. The lock key is the raw frontmatter `name` and the directory is `sanitize_name(name)`; they are two different strings (`crates/core/src/skills/install_fetched.rs:553` vs `:410`, and `name: PDF Tools` is a legal frontmatter name per `crates/skill/src/parser.rs:197-203`). Resolve the Master through DISCOVERY, never by probing `hub_dir.join(sanitize_name(name))`.
- Each Referrer path is **absent, or a symlink whose ONE-HOP target is that directory**.

Conformance is two syscalls, not one:

```
conformant(referrer, master) :=
    Linker::is_link(referrer)                                  // lstat: not a real directory
 && canonicalize(referrer) == canonicalize(master)             // endpoint
 && !symlink_metadata(referrer.parent().join(read_link(referrer)))?.is_symlink()
                                                               // the one hop lands on the Master, not on another Referrer
```

`symlink_metadata` alone decides nothing about a target: a healthy link, a two-hop chain and a dangling link all report `is_symlink = true` (verified). The chain is not hypothetical — npx `createSymlink` (`installer.ts:225-231`) rewrites `~/.claude/skills/<n>` to point at `.agents/skills/<n>` on every write, and a chain passes every endpoint comparison in the tree today (`crates/cli/src/commands/doctor.rs:236-243`, `crates/core/src/manager/skill.rs:363-369` and `:1220-1232`, `crates/core/src/skills/removal.rs:557-566`), so `doctor --verify-links` reports `verified` right up until `delete -a cline --yes` unlinks the middle hop and leaves claude — named nowhere in the command — dangling, which is precisely the state the ordering invariant exists to prevent. The third line rejects it; the OS resolves the intermediate `..` inside the join, so this is not the hand-rolled normalization AGENTS.md bans, and `resolve_existing` is NOT a substitute — it canonicalizes, so the chain resolves through and passes.

Put the predicate in ONE function beside `canonicalize_lenient` in `crates/core/src/skills/linker/classify.rs` and have all four sites above call it; patching them independently is the hand-mirroring AGENTS.md bans. Name the chain in `AgentLinkState` (`IndirectLink`) so `doctor --verify-links` reports it instead of certifying it.

One shape is NOT a violation: a lock-named **real directory at `.agents/skills/<n>` with `.aghub/<n>` absent** is the pre-migration state. It classifies as "legacy, migrate now", and every read path (`check`, `doctor`, `list`) and every preview must tolerate it on an unmigrated host. The other non-violations are enumerated in Policy 2.

Detection is comprehensive **of shape** — not of authorization. `absent` is legal and indistinguishable from a lost grant.

delete / prune-lock 要不要豁免 shape check：原發現說要豁免（否則使用者沒有清理手段），複查說**不要**豁免（delete 會 remove_dir_all 掉 npx 寫的唯一副本）。**裁決：兩邊都不採用，把前提移除**。Policy 2 改成 quarantine-by-rename 之後，fork 的位元組不會消失，delete 於是自然變成「先隔離、再刪除」，既不需要豁免清單，也不需要新增一個 repair 動詞來當唯一出口 —— 順帶解掉「repair 必須取得那個會在其內部拒絕它的 guard」這個循環。

Policy 2 的 repair 判準：spec 說 hash 相等就靜默折疊；一個發現說改成三值＋隔離；另一個發現說乾脆永遠 rename 不比對。**裁決：三值＋隔離，但 hash 是對照 lock entry 的 skillFolderHash，不是對照 Master**。永遠 rename 會把「使用者自己的同名真目錄／npx fork 之後又被人編輯過」這種 AGENTS.md 明文合法的 shadow，在沒問過的情況下從 5 個 agent 底下搬走。對照 lock hash 剛好把「npx 寫的、沒人動過」與「有人動過」分開，而且兩個分支都是無損的，所以 hash 對 node_modules／mode bits 盲目在這裡無害（它不決定任何刪除）。

授權紀錄要不要落地、放哪：一個發現說 sidecar 必須放在 .aghub/ **之外**（避免 npx folder hash 漂移），另一個說必須放在 .aghub/ **之內**（避免 AGENTS.md 三個 app-data root 陷阱）。**裁決：兩者皆非，這一版不加 sidecar**。migration 的 referrer 集合從磁碟＋descriptor 推導（不需要紀錄），而 Policy 1 真正 load-bearing 的那半改用「回報這次寫入送達了哪些 Referrer、空集合就明講」關掉，同樣不需要紀錄。若日後仍要記錄，兩個約束其實可同時滿足：`.aghub/grants.json`（在 .aghub/ 下、但不在 .aghub/<name>/ 內，npx 只 hash 後者）。
「bump lock version 來乾淨加欄位」：**否決並寫進 spec 當否決紀錄** —— npx readSkillLock 對 version < CURRENT 直接回 createEmptyLockFile()，使用者整份 lock 蒸發。

spec §Contract 的 slot-dedup ＋ agent_results.len() == target_agents.len() 斷言 vs Q1 的「這個 bug 不存在」。**裁決：Q1 勝，整段刪除**（已驗證：symlink_dirs 未 dedup、attribution 以目錄為 key 而非位置，8 個共用槽 agent 今天就都得到 installed: true）。連帶否決 discovery 的「先 dedup agent_skills_dirs」建議 —— 正是那個 dedup 才會逼出這條斷言。

doctor 的第三種狀態怎麼命名／放哪：spec 說 redefine orphanMaster；Q1 說新增 Withheld。**裁決：新增狀態，但名字取 `Unlinked`**。redefine orphanMaster 指錯地方（它以 !tracked 為條件，這個狀態根本走不到）；而 Withheld 是以意圖命名，會和同一份文件裡「lock 不記錄任何 per-skill 授權」自相矛盾 —— 用可觀察的事實命名。

conformance 判準：spec 說一次 symlink_metadata；一個發現說改成 read_link 的字面比對；複查說那正是 AGENTS.md 禁止的 lexical walk，而 resolve_existing 也不能代打（它會把鏈解穿過去）。**裁決：兩次 syscall —— endpoint canonicalize（沿用現有四個站點的比法）＋ 對 one-hop target 做一次 lstat 擋掉兩跳鏈**，`..` 交給 OS 在 join 裡解，不碰禁令。
canonicalize_lenient：discovery 說「保留函式、補一個直接測試」vs Q1 說「改成 resolve_existing 的 delegate」。**裁決：Q1 勝** —— 改動之後同一個比較同時決定授權、移除判準與 transfer 保護集，AGENTS.md 的「路徑正規化只有一個家」直接適用。
amp/kimi 的 global 寫入路徑要不要搬到 get_universal_skills_path()：提案說搬；Q3 說凍結。**裁決：凍結**。在新佈局下 Referrer 是唯一遞送機制，賭錯 vendor 的 XDG 行為＝那兩個 agent 完全失去技能，而不是今天那條無害的多餘讀取路徑；只在 READ arm 同時列出兩種拼法即可。
